summary: Complete target-level consolidation of global centres, termination, principalization, embedded resolution and resolved-open/local-isomorphism compatibility. Seven accepted aggregate targets and two accepted native finite-output constructions already own this mathematics. They are imported by canonical IDs and packet hashes, with eleven direct support nodes, rather than planned again. The reader specifies all nine targets, fourteen inherited API items and twelve inherited tests. R09.7c is planned, not closed: three inherited supplier contracts and the finite-tower/pair/comparison implementation obligations remain. No new node or implementation claim is made.

sources.title: Canonical desingularization in characteristic zero by blowing up the maximum strata of a local invariant
sources.authors: Edward Bierstone and Pierre D. Milman
sources.edition: Inventiones mathematicae 128 (1997), 207–302; full 96-page published article, printed pagination
readSections: Closed-point convention and simultaneous-coordinate condition, p. 213; principalization Theorem 1.10 and its setup, pp. 216–217; Theorem 1.14 and Remarks 1.15–1.16, pp. 219–221; Remark 1.18, p. 225.
Terminal monomial descent and Remark 6.17, pp. 259–260; global maximum algorithm and 10.3, pp. 283–285; higher-codimension geometric lemmas and Theorem 11.14, pp. 288–291.
Theorems 12.2 and 12.4, subset-intersection bad locus, Lemmas 12.5, 12.7–12.8, their proof and Example 12.9, pp. 292–296; embedding comparisons and Theorem 13.2 with its proof, pp. 296–298.

sources.locator: Remarks 1.15–1.16, pp. 220–221; 10.3 and algorithm, pp. 284–285; Theorem 11.14, pp. 290–291; closed-point convention, p. 213
sources.match: Semicoherent maximal strata give compatible smooth centres; the labelled boundary and the treatment of incomparable maximal Hilbert–Samuel values determine the global choice

importedTargets.scopeClarification: The prescribed closed unresolved locus is invariant-saturated for the selected variant, as in Remarks 10.3: an invariant equality stratum meeting it lies in it. This is not a smooth-centre assertion for an arbitrary closed subset of a stratum.

sources.match: Stabilization of the invariant, bounded positive denominators, finite dimension and monomial mass descent prove termination of the algebraic algorithm
Starting from empty boundary, admissible blowups turn an ideal into an invertible normal-crossings monomial ideal and preserve the complement of its support

sources.locator: Theorem 11.4, p. 288; Corollary 11.9 and Lemma 11.11, p. 289; Proposition 11.13, p. 290; Theorem 11.14, pp. 290–291
sources.match: The dimension and component analysis turns the general invariant algorithm into embedded resolution of a reduced scheme, with centres over its original singular locus

importedTargets.scopeClarification: The nonreduced extension in Theorem 11.14 has smooth reduction and locally constant Hilbert–Samuel function of the possibly nonreduced endpoint at closed points. The native embedded tower here has reduced input.

sources.locator: Definition of Σ* and subset-intersection criterion, pp. 292–293; Theorem 12.4, Lemma 12.5 and Remarks 12.6, p. 293
sources.match: Simultaneous normal crossings is equivalent to every boundary-subset intersection having the expected smooth dimension; embedding-dimension defects define the closed unresolved locus

importedTargets.scopeClarification: The embedding-dimension inequality uses closed points, as on p. 213. On all scheme points define the closed defect loci by failure of independence of the restricted boundary differentials in the relative cotangent space on a smooth component. Its relative dimension is locally constant; local-ring dimension on all scheme points is not.

sources.locator: Theorem 12.2, p. 292; Theorem 12.4 and proof, pp. 293–295; Lemmas 12.7–12.8, p. 294; Example 12.9, pp. 295–296
sources.match: The second resolution phase cleans up a smooth pair using centres in its unresolved locus; it preserves resolved points even when ordinary multiplicity alone would choose unsuitable centres

sources.locator: Remarks 13.1, p. 296; Theorem 13.2 and proof, pp. 297–298
sources.match: The normalized invariant removes dependence on local smooth embeddings and glues a resolution that lifts isomorphisms between open subschemes

importedTargets.scopeClarification: Whole-tower isomorphisms concern the intrinsic strict transforms. Ambient-pair isomorphisms induce ambient-tower isomorphisms; closed smooth ambient enlargements induce compatible ambient embeddings, with isomorphisms on the intrinsic transforms.

sources.match: Principalization supplies a finite centre-by-centre witness, an invertible total ideal with normal-crossings support, and a unit weak transform.

sources.locator: Theorem 11.14 and following paragraph, pp. 290–291; Theorems 12.2, 12.4, 13.2, pp. 292–294, 297–298
sources.match: The finite embedded witness carries iterative strict transforms and prescribed-open preservation; local isomorphisms lift through the entire towers.

importedTargets.scopeClarification: Theorem 13.2 compares the intrinsic strict-transform towers under open isomorphisms. Ambient towers are compared by isomorphisms only for ambient-pair isomorphisms; changing the smooth ambient embedding can instead give comparison embeddings.

requests.need: Reuse Layer 4 ordinary Rees/relative-Proj blowups with native finite-type quasi-coherent centre ideals, universal property, projectivity/properness, complement isomorphism, exceptional ideal, scheme-theoretic strict transform, standard charts and flat base change. Identify a regular-pivot chart with R[I/x] inside R[1/x]. This requests the existing general blowup interface, not another blowup or characteristic-zero resolution from the arithmetic-surface theorem.

Supply the residual finite-type coherent ideal localization/completion/quotient comparisons, regular-to-completed coordinate and Jacobian calculus over the actual closed-point residue field, local smooth embeddings and scheme open gluing. The existing SF.0/jacobson-finite-type and SF.0/etale-coordinates nodes give exact target pointers for those two subcontracts; their supplier packet has review status needs_changes, so they are not credited as accepted or implemented here. No existing node was found that supplies this whole remaining comparison/gluing contract.

For the imported SNC-boundary input, reuse the current native Scheme.IdealSheafData.IsEffectiveCartier and supply the remaining unrestricted-scheme additive Cartier-divisor/ideal-product dictionary, with pullback under regularity of the pulled-back local equations. A blowup need not be flat; use regular-pivot chart embeddings for its exceptional and transformed divisor equations.

remaining: Discharge the inherited ordinary-blowup, local algebra/gluing and Cartier supplier contracts recorded in requests; exact existing owner nodes are preserved.

Implement the imported R09.7a finite-tower carrier and populate both output constructions from the finite algorithm, retaining native centre ideals, coordinate permissibility, total/weak/strict transforms, all surviving and born labels and the prescribed-open identifications.

Prove the smooth-pair resolved-open refinement and unique comparisons through every restricted tower, including centre-ideal overlap equations, ambient-embedding independence, deletion of empty-centre steps and the identity/composition/cocycle laws. A final proper smooth endpoint alone does not discharge these contracts.

Carry out the Lean proofs of the canonical R09.7 and R09.7a targets and their API/tests. The compact suggested file states only a native endpoint consequence and elementary chart/pullback checks; it does not implement the invariant, SNC predicates or finite towers.

checked.note: Read Remarks 1.15–1.16, 10.3 and the global algorithm. Made explicit that the prescribed closed bad locus is invariant-saturated for the selected variant; arbitrary closed subsets are not allowed. Checked coherent centre gluing, chronological labels, all incomparable maxima and the three API/tests.

Theorem 1.14(2),(4), pp. 219–220, terminal monomial calculation pp. 259–260 and algorithm pp. 284–285 support the finite quasi-compact algorithm. Imported realized Hilbert–Samuel stabilization is retained as an accepted boundary, not replaced by well-foundedness of arbitrary functions.

Theorem 1.10, pp. 216–217, Remark 1.18, p. 225, and §6 support the empty-boundary, generically nonzero coherent ideal contract, invertible monomial total transform, unit weak transform and preservation outside the initial support. No resolution theorem is supplied by the ordinary-blowup owner.

Read Theorem 11.4 through Theorem 11.14, pp. 288–291. Fixed Theorem/Corollary/Lemma labels for 11.4/11.9/11.11. Clarified that local constancy concerns the Hilbert–Samuel function of the possibly nonreduced endpoint at closed points, while its reduction is smooth. Reduced native tower and original regular-open preservation remain explicit.

Read Theorem 12.4, Lemma 12.5 and Remarks 12.6, p. 293. Restricted the local embedding-dimension formula to closed points and supplied the relative cotangent/Jacobian-minor formulation for all scheme points; relative dimension, rather than all local-ring dimensions, is locally constant. Checked every-subset criterion and all three API/tests.

Read Theorems 12.2/12.4, Lemmas 12.7/12.8 and Example 12.9, pp. 292–296. Residual-product induction plus the stronger new-exceptional monomial procedure stays in the pair bad locus and preserves initially resolved points. The two-step z=xy example and ordinary regular-open distinction are correct.

Read Remarks 13.1 and Theorem 13.2 with proof, pp. 296–298. Clarified that the intrinsic towers are isomorphic; ambient enlargements yield ambient comparison embeddings. Checked normalized invariant independence, overlap ideals, unique lifts, empty-step reindexing and cocycles. No arbitrary smooth functoriality is claimed.

Finite witness imports the accepted finite-blowup-tower and principalization nodes. Verified the four APIs and three tests, native contravariant pullback, total/weak distinction, and nonempty Cartier identity steps with retained labels. The coordinate-monomial certificate is an output witness, not a claim about the selected algorithm.

Read Theorem 11.14 and Theorems 12.2/12.4/13.2. Clarified intrinsic versus ambient tower comparisons. Verified native kernel strict-closure convention with quasi-compactness, permissible centres, commuting squares, endpoint/preserved-open APIs and the three tests distinguishing strict from total inverse image.
